title: En aras de: justificar una decisión con un objetivo superior

sections.content: En aras de (for the sake of, in the interest of) frames a decision as serving some larger, supposedly higher goal -- common in historical writing that wants to name the stated justification without necessarily endorsing it. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En aras de proyectar una imagen de legitimidad institucional, Pinochet convocó un plebiscito nacional en octubre de 1988.
items.english: For the sake of projecting an image of institutional legitimacy, Pinochet called a national plebiscite in October 1988.

items.spanish: La oposición logró, en aras de la unidad, superar sus propias divisiones internas.
items.english: The opposition managed, for the sake of unity, to overcome its own internal divisions.

items.spanish: Pinochet permaneció como comandante en jefe, en aras de una transición que muchos consideraron incompleta.
items.english: Pinochet remained as commander-in-chief, for the sake of a transition many considered incomplete.

items.spanish: En aras de la estabilidad política, algunos partidos aceptaron condiciones que, en otro contexto, habrían rechazado.
items.english: For the sake of political stability, some parties accepted conditions that, in another context, they would have rejected.

sections.content: En aras de often signals, at least implicitly, that the stated goal is worth scrutinizing -- similar to so pretexto de but softer, since the goal named may be genuine rather than a mere excuse.
